findings.text: Current CPU vector pool can be brought into service and later withdrawn. First activation derives per CPU free count from configured size less managed and system overlap. Service changes adjust shared free total and online map count.

Shared free total reflects aggregate of per CPU free counts for online maps. Online transition adds local free count, offline transition subtracts it. Assignment and allocation reduce both levels and raise allocation totals, while unmanaged release restores free counts.

Per CPU pool moves from uninitialized to initialized on first online, then between online and offline. Initialization happens once and fixes starting free count. Online state gates eligibility for allocation and inclusion in shared totals.

Vector search stays inside configured window and avoids vectors already claimed as managed reservations, system use, or prior allocations. Search combines those occupied sets into scratch space and seeks a free span of requested length. Failure is signaled by a position at or beyond window end, success records the span in the appropriate per CPU set.

Unmanaged choice prefers the eligible online CPU with the largest free count. Managed choice prefers the eligible online CPU with the smallest managed allocation count. Offline CPUs and those not improving the current best are skipped. A distinct sentinel indicates that no candidate exists.

A system vector can be marked in the shared system set. Replacement mode converts a prior local allocation into system use and adjusts allocation totals. Overlap between the chosen bit and the allocation window is counted for future availability derivation. Use is confined to early single map bringup unless replacing.

System marking traps misuse when the bit lies outside matrix capacity or when more than one map is online without replacement. Replacement also traps when the expected prior local allocation is absent.

Managed capacity is reserved on every CPU of a mask, allocated later on one least loaded online member, and finally released and unreserved. Reservation failure rolls back earlier successes in the same request. Removal returns one reserved but unallocated slot, allocation consumes such a slot, and free drops the allocation and its managed charge.

Reservation raises per CPU managed count and, when online, lowers free counts at both levels. Removal lowers managed count and restores free counts. Managed allocation raises allocation totals and managed allocation charge without changing free counts beyond reservation, while unmanaged paths adjust free counts directly.

Fresh vectors can be allocated on the best eligible CPU with optional consumption of a prior global reservation. A caller chosen vector can be recorded on the current CPU. Global demand can be tracked separately through increment and decrement operations, with a warning when demand reaches current availability.

Empty CPU masks are rejected as invalid. Absence of an eligible online CPU or of a free vector yields a no space error. Managed reservation maps allocation failure to no space after cleanup of partial progress.

Explicit assignment and release validate that the vector lies inside the allocation window and that booking state transitions correctly. Out of range, double booking, or release of an unbooked vector triggers a one time warning and leaves counters unchanged.

Current availability can be queried globally or with the local pool excluded to model CPU removal. Global reservation total and net allocated count excluding managed charge are observable. Debug output reports global totals, system weight, and a per CPU table of availability and allocation counters plus allocation bitmap.
Matrix debug reporting holds CPU read protection while iterating online CPUs and reading per CPU counters.

This path applies a pending CPU set to an interrupt that allows migration. Success clears the pending set. Several situations leave it unchanged or abort early, including absent pending flag, per CPU scope, empty set, missing affinity support, or lack of overlap with online CPUs. Temporary busy status reflags the work and preserves the set for a later attempt.

This wrapper resolves top level interrupt data, ignores disabled interrupts, and preserves masking discipline around pending move handling. It masks only when previously unmasked and restores that state afterwards.
Eligibility for process context migration is determined from top level interrupt data through a helper predicate.

Calling the masked move path for CPU local interrupts indicates a caller error and triggers a diagnostic. Edge sensitive hardware motivates masking before reprogramming, a responsibility placed on the caller.
Masked move handling requires the descriptor lock to be held on entry, enforced by an assertion.
Device MSI state uses properties for flags, mutex for serialization, __domains for per domain storage, and __iter_idx for cached iteration progress across calls.
Range descriptor uses domid to select domain, first and last to bound the interval, and nirqs to count interrupts.
Sentinel marking invalid or exhausted descriptor iteration is one less than the largest unsigned long value.
Per domain descriptor store capacity equals the largest valid descriptor index plus one.

Descriptors can be inserted at a chosen index with type specific data carried over, freed over an index interval, or created as single vector entries over an interval with validation. Creation failure releases partial progress and reports memory or validation errors.

Mutation and iteration of descriptor stores require holding the device MSI mutex, checked by ownership assertions. Dedicated lock and unlock helpers manage this mutex, with unlock also invalidating cached iteration state.

Iteration starts at zero, advances stepwise with an upper bound check, and scans forward from the cached position for the next entry matching a filter. Reaching the end or finding no match yields null and parks the cache at the sentinel. Unlock also parks the cache at the sentinel.
Stored message contents can be copied out by descriptor reference or by interrupt number lookup.
Managed release ensures domain removal and store destruction with emptiness warnings, leaving the device pointer cleared.

Setup guarantees initialized device MSI state with per domain stores, sysfs grouping, mutex protection, and managed lifetime. Existing state makes the call succeed without change. A compatible preassigned domain is inherited into the default slot. Allocation or grouping failures prevent linkage.
One build configuration registers an interrupt sysfs group on the device, while the alternate configuration provides a no operation that reports success.

Interrupt number lookup by domain and index returns zero for missing state or out of range inputs. PCI MSI collapses to the first descriptor with offset arithmetic bounded by used vector count, while other cases use one descriptor per index and require a nonzero stored interrupt.
Sysfs exposure uses an initially empty attribute list under a group named msi_irqs.
Mode reporting emits msix for PCI devices with extended capability enabled, otherwise msi.
Population creates sysfs entries for associated descriptors lacking them and aborts on first error. Destruction removes entries for all descriptors regardless of association.

Affinity changes delegate to the parent and, unless already complete, refresh hardware message state. Activation composes and writes the message, deactivation writes a cleared message. Allocation rejects duplicate hardware mappings, delegates to the parent when present, initializes each interrupt with unwinding of earlier successes and parent resources on failure. Release invokes per interrupt teardown when defined then frees parent resources. Translation requires provider support and otherwise reports unsupported operation.

Level signaling requires capability flags in both domain and chip state. When either is absent, the second message slot must remain clear, with violation reported as a warning. Message writes go through the chip callback.

Removal ensures provider teardown, domain deregistration, and template release with the device slot cleared. Absent or incompatible domains make the call return without action. Firmware references are released when the removed domain carried them.
Device domain teardown and interrupt number lookup use scoped protection for descriptor access.
Debug reporting for MSI state prints cached high and low address parts plus data payload when a descriptor is associated, otherwise emits nothing.
